cost: O(format bytes + expanded atoms + repeated segment/flag scans + emitted bytes); repeated conversion/flag scans can require O(format length * expanded atoms) work even with small output. String-to-code expansion and requested width/precision can dominate allocations. No resource bound or useful percent surrogate for exact text.
description: Output registration and C-like format parser/cycler; scalar numeric formatting and num2str/mat2str conversions.
forward: sprintf_impl parses format, flattens real numeric matrices column-major to atoms, then cycles segments until atoms consumed. Strings under numeric conversions expand to Unicode scalar codes. fprintf formatted-string branch writes the completed string through Interp.out and returns UTF-8 byte count only for nargout>0. A scalar nonchar first argument is ignored as fid only when followed by a char format. The numeric-first fallback formats all arguments with %g\n and returns no values even for nargout>0.
inverse: Unsupported atom types exclude any successful formatted output even for a literal-only format because atoms is called first. Empty argument queue excludes numeric substitution; empty specs can still contribute width padding.

Rendered strings admit many inputs: integer/float atoms with same formatting, varying matrix shapes with identical real storage, ignored imaginary components and fid values in the qualifying scalar-fid/char-format branch. No inverse recovers those discarded components.
limitations: Partial source-bound model, not semantic proof
Finite synthetic fixtures only; frozen suites/external measurement unexecuted
state: Numeric atoms follow m.re storage, not printed row order; char matrices are one string atom. num2str default aligns columns while mat2str assembles row syntax.
